subject: Bald Eagle
fact: Bald eagles build some of the largest nests made by any bird.

subject: Golden Eagle
fact: Golden eagles use sharp eyesight to spot prey from high in the sky.

subject: Peregrine Falcon
fact: Peregrine falcons can dive at extraordinary speeds while hunting.

subject: Red-Tailed Hawk
fact: Red-tailed hawks are often seen soaring in wide circles over open land.

subject: Osprey
fact: Ospreys are fish-eating raptors with feet specially adapted for gripping slippery prey.

subject: Barn Owl
fact: Barn owls have heart-shaped faces that help direct sound toward their ears.

subject: Snowy Owl
fact: Snowy owls have thick feathers that help them survive Arctic winters.

subject: Great Horned Owl
fact: Great horned owls have feather tufts that look like horns.

subject: Flamingo
fact: Flamingos get much of their pink color from pigments in the food they eat.

subject: Peacock
fact: Male peafowl can spread long colorful tail feathers into a huge fan.

subject: Scarlet Macaw
fact: Scarlet macaws use strong curved beaks to crack nuts and seeds.

subject: Blue-and-Yellow Macaw
fact: Blue-and-yellow macaws are large parrots that live in parts of South America.

subject: Toco Toucan
fact: Toco toucans have enormous colorful bills that are surprisingly lightweight.

subject: Amazon Parrot
fact: Amazon parrots are social birds known for loud calls and strong voices.

subject: Cockatoo
fact: Cockatoos can raise and lower the crest of feathers on top of their heads.

subject: African Grey Parrot
fact: African grey parrots are famous for learning and imitating many different sounds.

subject: Ruby-Throated Hummingbird
fact: Hummingbirds can hover by beating their wings very quickly.

subject: Belted Kingfisher
fact: Kingfishers often dive from perches to catch fish in the water.

subject: Pileated Woodpecker
fact: Pileated woodpeckers chip large holes into dead trees while searching for insects.

subject: American Robin
fact: American robins often hunt for earthworms on lawns and open ground.

subject: Blue Jay
fact: Blue jays can imitate the calls of some hawks.

subject: Northern Cardinal
fact: Male northern cardinals are bright red while females are mostly warm brown.

subject: House Sparrow
fact: House sparrows often live close to people in towns and cities.

subject: American Goldfinch
fact: Male American goldfinches turn bright yellow during the breeding season.

subject: Canary
fact: Canaries are small finches known for their musical songs.

subject: American Crow
fact: Crows are highly intelligent birds that can solve problems and remember faces.

subject: Common Raven
fact: Ravens are large members of the crow family and can perform playful aerial rolls.

subject: Black-Billed Magpie
fact: Magpies are bold black-and-white birds with long tails.

subject: Rock Pigeon
fact: Pigeons can find their way home from long distances.

subject: Mourning Dove
fact: Mourning doves make a soft cooing call that sounds almost like a whistle.

subject: Herring Gull
fact: Gulls are adaptable birds that can live along coasts, lakes, and cities.

subject: Brown Pelican
fact: Brown pelicans plunge into the water to catch fish.

subject: Atlantic Puffin
fact: Puffins use their colorful bills to hold several small fish at once.

subject: Wandering Albatross
fact: Wandering albatrosses have some of the widest wingspans of any living bird.

subject: Emperor Penguin
fact: Emperor penguins are the largest living penguins.

subject: Ostrich
fact: Ostriches are the world's largest living birds and cannot fly.

subject: Emu
fact: Emus are large flightless Australian birds with long powerful legs.

subject: Southern Cassowary
fact: Cassowaries have a helmet-like casque on top of their heads.

subject: Kiwi
fact: Kiwis are flightless birds with nostrils near the tips of their long bills.

subject: Wild Turkey
fact: Wild turkeys can fly short distances despite their heavy bodies.

subject: Chicken
fact: Chickens use different calls to communicate about food and danger.

subject: Mallard Duck
fact: Male mallards usually have glossy green heads.

subject: Canada Goose
fact: Canada geese fly in V-shaped formations that can help save energy.

subject: Mute Swan
fact: Swans have long necks and powerful wings.

subject: Sandhill Crane
fact: Sandhill cranes perform energetic dances with jumps and wing flaps.

subject: White Stork
fact: White storks build large stick nests on tall structures and trees.

subject: Great Blue Heron
fact: Great blue herons stand very still before striking quickly at fish.

subject: Great Egret
fact: Great egrets have long necks and spear-shaped bills for catching prey.

subject: Scarlet Ibis
fact: Scarlet ibises become red from pigments in the crustaceans they eat.

subject: Roseate Spoonbill
fact: Spoonbills sweep their flat bills side to side through shallow water to find food.

subject: Great Hornbill
fact: Hornbills have large bills topped by a hollow structure called a casque.

subject: Hoopoe
fact: Hoopoes can raise a crown-like fan of feathers on their heads.

subject: European Bee-Eater
fact: Bee-eaters catch flying insects in the air and often perch together.

subject: Secretary Bird
fact: Secretary birds hunt on the ground and use powerful legs to strike prey.

subject: Laughing Kookaburra
fact: Kookaburras are kingfishers famous for loud calls that sound like laughter.

subject: Greater Roadrunner
fact: Roadrunners can sprint quickly across the ground while hunting small animals.

subject: California Quail
fact: California quail have a curved feather plume that bobs above the forehead.

subject: Ring-Necked Pheasant
fact: Male ring-necked pheasants have bright colors and very long tails.

subject: Gray Partridge
fact: Gray partridges are ground birds that often stay in groups called coveys.

subject: Common Loon
fact: Loons are excellent divers with legs set far back on their bodies for swimming.
